name: Alaska
nameStory: From the Aleut word 'Alaxsxaq' - roughly 'the thing the sea crashes against,' meaning the mainland. To people living out on the Aleutian islands, Alaska was simply the big land the waves break on.
capitalStory: Juneau is the only state capital in America you cannot drive to. No road connects it to the rest of the continent, so legislators fly or take a ferry to work. It is named for Joe Juneau, a prospector who struck gold there in 1880.

majorFeatures.name: Denali
majorFeatures.note: Highest peak in North America, 20,310 ft

majorFeatures.name: Yukon River
majorFeatures.note: Runs 1,980 miles from Canada to the Bering Sea

majorFeatures.name: Brooks Range
majorFeatures.note: Arctic mountain wall across the north

funFacts: The US bought Alaska from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million, about two cents an acre. Newspapers called it 'Seward's Folly.'
Alaska is bigger than Texas, California, and Montana combined.
It has more coastline than all the other 49 states put together.
The Aleutians cross the 180th meridian, which technically makes Alaska both the westernmost and the easternmost state.
It borders no US state - only Canada.
whyItMatters: As Arctic sea ice retreats, Alaska sits beside newly navigable shipping routes and contested seabed oil, making it a focus of US, Russian, and Chinese strategic interest.
